claims.statement: The Stoep is a tormenting spirit (kwelgeest) of Gelderland (Gelderse overleveringen) that leaps onto lone people's backs (rug), turns lead-heavy (loodzwaar) and vanishes when the walker (wandelaar) reaches houses (huizen).
claims.statement_id: Stoep adalah roh pengganggu (kwelgeest) Gelderland (Gelderse overleveringen) yang melompat ke punggung (rug) orang sendirian, menjadi seberat timah (loodzwaar), dan lenyap saat pejalan (wandelaar) sampai di rumah (huizen).
claims.quote: De Stoep is een kwelgeest uit Gelderse overleveringen. Hij zou op de rug van eenzame mensen springen, om zichzelf vervolgens loodzwaar te maken, maar verdwijnt zodra de wandelaar huizen bereikt. De geplaagde is dan alleen wel doodop.

claims.statement: The Stoep is related (verwant) to the Ossaert, Blauwe Gerrit, Lange Wapper and Kludde.
claims.statement_id: Stoep berkerabat (verwant) dengan Ossaert, Blauwe Gerrit, Lange Wapper, dan Kludde.
claims.quote: Stoep is verwant aan de Ossaert, Blauwe Gerrit, Lange Wapper en Kludde.

claims.statement: Tomtormar, husormar or gårdsormar were grass snakes (snokar, Natrix natrix, Coronella austriaca) near houses (hus) and barns (ladugårdar), given milk (mjölk).
claims.statement_id: Tomtormar, husormar, atau gårdsormar adalah ular rumput (snokar, Natrix natrix, Coronella austriaca) di dekat rumah (hus) dan kandang (ladugårdar) yang diberi susu (mjölk).
claims.quote: Tomtormar, husormar eller gårdsormar kallades i äldre tid de snokar (oftast Natrix natrix men även Hasselsnok, Coronella austriaca) som uppehöll sig i närheten av hus och ladugårdar och som gårdsfolket brukade ge mjölk.

claims.statement: In folk belief (folktron) well-treated snakes (ormarna) brought livestock luck (boskapslyckan) and protected against lightning (åsknedslag); a tomtorm must not be killed (dödas).
claims.statement_id: Menurut kepercayaan rakyat (folktron), ular (ormarna) yang dirawat baik membawa untung ternak (boskapslyckan) dan melindungi dari petir (åsknedslag); tomtorm tak boleh dibunuh (dödas).
claims.quote: Om ormarna behandlades väl skulle de enligt folktron befrämja boskapslyckan samt skydda gården mot olyckor, exempelvis åsknedslag. En tomtorm fick absolut inte dödas; om så skedde kunde gården drabbas av stor olycka.

claims.statement: Belief (Tron) in tomtormar was widespread in Scandinavia (Skandinavien), Finland and the Baltic (Baltikum).
claims.statement_id: Kepercayaan (Tron) pada tomtormar tersebar di Skandinavia (Skandinavien), Finlandia (Finland), dan Baltik (Baltikum).
claims.quote: Tron på tomtormar har varit vida utbredd i hela Skandinavien, Finland och Baltikum

claims.statement: Olaus Magnus (1555): house snakes (husormar) in the north were household gods (husgudar, penates), given milk, played with children (barnen) and slept in the cradle (vaggan) as guardians (väktare).
claims.statement_id: Olaus Magnus (1555): ular rumah (husormar) di utara dianggap dewa rumah (husgudar, penates), diberi susu, bermain dengan anak (barnen), dan tidur di buaian (vaggan) sebagai penjaga (väktare).
claims.quote: Det finns även husormar, vilka längst upp i norr betraktas som husgudar (penates): de få dricka ko- eller fårmjölk, leka med barnen inomhus och ses ofta sova i vaggan som trogna väktare.

claims.statement: Michael Heberer (1592): the children (barnen) ate porridge (gröt) on the floor, and two snakes (ormar) came and ate from the same dish (fat).
claims.statement_id: Michael Heberer (1592): anak-anak (barnen) makan bubur (gröt) di lantai, lalu dua ular (ormar) datang dan makan dari piring (fat) yang sama.
claims.quote: Medan vi väntade på att bekomma något att äta, sutto barnen på jorden och förtärde sin gröt. Då kröpo två ormar dit och åto med barnen utur samma fat.

claims.statement: The snakes (Ormarna) were given warm milk (spenvarm mjölk) and called with "Snokera!"; other names were Långfiskene and Långpisen.
claims.statement_id: Ular-ular (Ormarna) diberi susu hangat (spenvarm mjölk) dan dipanggil makan dengan seruan "Snokera!"; sebutan lain: Långfiskene dan Långpisen.
claims.quote: Ormarna skulle ha spenvarm mjölk för att trivas, och ibland kallades de till måltiden med lockrop: Snokera! sno-kera! Andra tilltal har varit: Långfiskene (”Långfiskarna”) och Långpisen (”Långkatterna”).

claims.statement: Older scholars (Äldre forskare) saw the milk offering as a remnant of a pagan snake cult (hednisk ormkult), but present-day historians (Nutida historiker) doubt snakes were worshipped in Sweden (Sverige).
claims.statement_id: Peneliti lama (Äldre forskare) melihat pemberian susu sebagai sisa kultus ular kafir (hednisk ormkult), tetapi sejarawan masa kini (Nutida historiker) meragukan ular dipuja di Swedia (Sverige).
claims.quote: Äldre forskare såg framsättandet av mjölk till tomtormen som en sista rest av en uråldrig hednisk ormkult, som de också fann antydd i runstenarnas drakslingor och djurornamentik. Nutida historiker betvivlar dock starkt att ormar har dyrkats i Sverige.

claims.statement: Žaltys (grass snake) is a household spirit of Lithuanian mythology in Lithuania.
claims.statement_id: Žaltys (ular rumput, grass snake) adalah roh rumah (household spirit) dalam mitologi Lituania (Lithuania, Lithuanian).
claims.quote: , literally: grass snake) is a household spirit in Lithuanian mythology.

claims.statement: Killing the žaltys brought great misfortunes on the household; one found in the field was given milk.
claims.statement_id: Membunuh žaltys mendatangkan malapetaka (misfortunes) bagi rumah tangga; žaltys yang ditemukan di ladang diberi susu (milk).
claims.quote: Killing the žaltys was said to bring great misfortunes upon the household. If a žaltys was found in the field, people gave it milk

claims.statement: Olaus Magnus's account is confirmed by the German traveller (tyske resenären) Michael Heberer von Bretten, who visited a farm in Småland in 1592.
claims.statement_id: Keterangan Olaus Magnus dikukuhkan pelancong Jerman (tyske resenären, German) Michael Heberer von Bretten yang pada 1592 mengunjungi pertanian di Småland.
claims.quote: Olaus Magnus uppgift bekräftas av den tyske resenären Michael Heberer von Bretten, som den 14 augusti 1592 besökte en gård i Linneryds socken i Småland

claims.statement: Records in the Nordiska museet collection show the custom of setting out milk (mjölk) for tomtormar spread across Skåne, Småland and up to Uppland.
claims.statement_id: Catatan koleksi Nordiska museet menunjukkan kebiasaan memberi susu (mjölk) kepada tomtormar tersebar di Skåne, Småland, hingga Uppland.
claims.quote: Av uppteckningar i Nordiska museets folkminnessamling framgår att seden att sätta fram mjölk åt gårdens tomtormar har varit utbredd i Skåne, Småland, Bohuslän, Dalsland, Väster- och Östergötland, Södermanland, Närke, Uppland och Västmanland.

claims.statement: The Uhaml is a spirit of German folktales in Bohemia and Silesia (now Czech Republic and Poland), especially Iglau; an airy sprite, ghost or demonic bird with horse feet.
claims.statement_id: Uhaml dikenal di Bohemia dan Silesia (kini Republik Ceko dan Polandia; Czech Republic, Poland), terutama Iglau; roh udara, hantu, atau burung iblis berkaki kuda.
claims.quote: It was known among the former Germans of Bohemia and Silesia, now part of the Czech Republic and Poland respectively, particularly in the former Iglau language island of Bohemia. The Uhaml is an airy sprite, a ghost, or possibly some kind of demonic bird. Nothing is known about its appearance other than it having horse feet.

claims.statement: At night the Uhaml's call "Uhuhu!" is heard from the air; mockers who imitate it are chased until safe under the eaves.
claims.statement_id: Pada malam hari seruan Uhaml "Uhuhu!" terdengar dari udara; yang menirunya dikejar hingga aman di bawah atap.
claims.quote: At night, the Uhaml's call can be heard from the air: "Uhuhu!" People mocking it by imitating its call will be chased by the Uhaml until they are safe from it under the eaves.

claims.statement: In the forest the Uhaml (here female) may aufhocken, leaping on a passerby's back until the forest border.
claims.statement_id: Di hutan, Uhaml (di sini perempuan) dapat aufhocken, melompat ke punggung orang dan turun di tepi hutan.
claims.quote: In the forest, "she" (for the Uhaml is apparently imagined as female in this case only) might also aufhocken, i.e. leap on a passerby's back and let itself be carried, jumping down from "her" victim only upon reaching the forest border.

claims.statement: To ward off the Uhaml, three wood chips and a loaf are placed in the parlour; the Uhaml halves the bread and takes one half.
claims.statement_id: Untuk menangkal Uhaml, tiga serpih kayu dan roti diletakkan di ruang tamu; Uhaml membelah roti dan membawa separuhnya.
claims.quote: To ward off the Uhaml's evildoing, three chips of wood and a loaf of bread will be placed in the parlor. The Uhaml will enter the parlor, cut the bread in two halves and take one of them with it.

claims.statement: The Uhaml and other legendary creatures might be based on the Eurasian eagle-owl.
claims.statement_id: Uhaml dan makhluk legenda lain mungkin berasal dari burung hantu besar Eurasia (Eurasian eagle-owl).
claims.quote: The Uhaml and other legendary creatures might be based on the Eurasian eagle-owl.

claims.statement: The name Uhaml may be a Silesian form of unheimlich (eerie), or more likely from Uhu, the Eurasian eagle-owl.
claims.statement_id: Nama Uhaml mungkin bentuk dialek Silesia (Silesian) dari unheimlich (seram), atau lebih mungkin dari Uhu, burung hantu besar Eurasia (Eurasian eagle-owl).
claims.quote: The name Uhaml can be explained as a Silesian dialectal form of Standard German "unheimlich", meaning "eerie" or "uncanny", or can more likely be connected to the Eurasian eagle-owl, called "Uhu" in German with regard to its call.

claims.statement: In Lower Austria there is the Udl, a demonic bird on the Schlossberg slopes at Mödling whose call is an omen of war or disaster.
claims.statement_id: Di Lower Austria (Austria Hilir) ada Udl, burung iblis di lereng Schlossberg di Mödling yang seruannya pertanda perang atau bencana.
claims.quote: In Lower Austria, there is the Udl, a demonic kind of bird dwelling in the woods covering the slopes of the castle mountain (Schlossberg) in Mödling. Its hoarse, raucous call can be heard relentlessly at night. The call of the Udl is a true omen for war or other disasters.

claims.statement: In the Steigerwald in Franconia the Uhumännle haunts a stone cross on the Ebrach–Michelau path, shouting "uhu".
claims.statement_id: Di Steigerwald, Franconia, Uhumännle menghantui salib batu di jalan Ebrach ke Michelau sambil berseru "uhu".
claims.quote: In the Steigerwald in Franconia, there is a stone cross on the path from Ebrach to Michelau. There, the Uhumännle is haunting, a ghost known for its habit of shouting "uhu".

claims.statement: Those who imitate the Uhumännle's "uhu" are slapped by an invisible hand.
claims.statement_id: Orang yang meniru seruan "uhu" Uhumännle ditampar tangan tak kasatmata.
claims.quote: Those who mock it by imitating its "uhu" will get slapped by an invisible hand.

claims.statement: The Uhaml (das Uhaml, neuter) is a spirit of German folktales.
claims.statement_id: Uhaml (das Uhaml, netral) adalah roh dari cerita rakyat Jerman (German folktales).
claims.quote: The Uhaml (German: das Uhaml with neuter article; German: [ˈuːˌhaml̩] ) is a spirit from German folktales.

claims.statement: According to legend (legenden), Jätten Vist is a giant (jätte) who made Visingsö: returning from a feast (fest) in Västergötland to Småland, he threw a turf (tuva) into Vättern to step on; the hole became Landsjön.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda (legenden), Jätten Vist adalah raksasa (jätte) pencipta Visingsö: pulang dari pesta (fest) di Västergötland ke Småland, ia melempar gumpalan tanah (tuva) ke Vättern sebagai pijakan; bekasnya menjadi Landsjön.
claims.quote: Jätten Vist är enligt legenden en jätte som skapade Visingsö, då han och hans fru hade varit på fest i Västergötland och skulle kliva över Vättern tillbaka till Småland. Han tog då en stor tuva och kastade ut den i sjön för att kliva på, och den tuvan återfinns numera som Visingsö. Tuvan han tog blev då sjön Landsjön.

claims.statement: Since 1969 a sculpture (skulptur) by Calle Örnemark of Vist with his tuva stands on Strandvägen in Huskvarna; restored (restaurerades) before the artist's death in 2015.
claims.statement_id: Sejak 1969 patung (skulptur) karya Calle Örnemark tentang Vist dan tuva-nya berdiri di Strandvägen, Huskvarna; dipugar (restaurerades) sebelum sang seniman wafat 2015.
claims.quote: Sedan 1969 finns en skulptur av Calle Örnemark, föreställande jätten Vist med sin tuva, vid Strandvägen i Huskvarna. Den restaurerades ett par månader före konstnärens död sommaren 2015.

claims.statement: By legend a giant named Vist created Visingsö by throwing a lump of soil into the lake for his wife to step on.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, raksasa bernama Vist menciptakan Visingsö dengan melempar segumpal tanah ke danau sebagai pijakan istrinya.
claims.quote: According to legend, a giant named Vist created Visingsö by throwing a lump of soil into the lake so that his wife could use it to step over the lake.

claims.statement: By legend (legenden) the island (ön) was made by the giant (jätten) Vist as a step for his wife (fru) over Vättern; Vist himself needed only one step (ett steg).
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda (legenden), pulau (ön) itu diciptakan raksasa (jätten) Vist sebagai pijakan istrinya (fru) di Vättern; Vist sendiri hanya perlu satu langkah (ett steg).
claims.quote: Enligt legenden skapades ön av jätten Vist när han kastade ut en tuva i sjön för att hans fru skulle ha något att kliva på när hon tog sig över Vättern. Vist själv behövde bara ett steg för att komma över sjön.

claims.statement: Jätten Vist is mentioned in the first track (första spåret) Tror jag hittar hem on singer (sångaren) Lars Winnerbäck's album (skiva) Eldtuppen.
claims.statement_id: Jätten Vist disebut dalam lagu pertama (första spåret) Tror jag hittar hem di album (skiva) Eldtuppen karya penyanyi (sångaren) Lars Winnerbäck.
claims.quote: Jätten Vist omnämns i första spåret Tror jag hittar hem på sångaren Lars Winnerbäcks skiva Eldtuppen.

claims.statement: In folk belief (folktro) Vita Karin is a ghost (spöke) at Snogeholm Castle (Snogeholms slott).
claims.statement_id: Menurut kepercayaan rakyat (folktro), Vita Karin adalah hantu (spöke) di kastel Snogeholm (Snogeholms slott).
claims.quote: Vita Karin är enligt folktro ett spöke på Snogeholms slott.

claims.statement: In life she was called Lilla Karin, worked in the castle dining room (matsal) in the late 1700s, often scolded (skäll) for putting fingers (fingrarna) in the pies (pajerna).
claims.statement_id: Semasa hidup ia disebut Lilla Karin, bekerja di ruang makan (matsal) kastel akhir 1700-an, dan sering dimarahi (skäll) karena mencelupkan jari (fingrarna) ke pai (pajerna).
claims.quote: Hon ska ha kallats "Lilla Karin" när hon levde och arbetade i slottets matsal i slutet 1700-talet. Hon fick ofta skäll för att hon satte fingrarna i pajerna när hon bar dem.

claims.statement: A nobleman (adelsman) fancied her; others sent a false proposal letter (falskt friarbrev) and called her to a cave (grotta) outside the castle (slottet).
claims.statement_id: Seorang bangsawan (adelsman) menyukainya; orang lain mengirim surat lamaran palsu (falskt friarbrev) dan memanggilnya ke gua (grotta) di luar kastel (slottet).
claims.quote: En adelsman hade ett gott öga till henne, vilket fick andra att vilja spela henne ett spratt. De skickade ett falskt friarbrev till Karin, och bad henne komma till en grotta utanför slottet.

claims.statement: Karin sewed a wedding dress (brudklänning) from curtains (gardiner); five men (fem män) assaulted her, and next morning she was found dead (död), pale, in a white dress (vit klänning).
claims.statement_id: Karin menjahit gaun pengantin (brudklänning) dari tirai (gardiner); lima lelaki (fem män) menganiayanya, dan pagi berikutnya ia ditemukan mati (död), pucat, dalam gaun putih (vit klänning).
claims.quote: Karin sydde en brudklänning av sina gardiner och begav sig till möteplatsen. Istället för adelsmannen väntade fem män på henne, som våldförde sig på henne och misshandlade henne. Hon bars tillbaks till slottet, där man fann henne nästa morgon, död, likblek och i en vit klänning.

claims.statement: Her spirit (ande) appears as a white glow (vitt ljussken) or a white flash (vit blixt).
claims.statement_id: Arwahnya (ande) menampakkan diri sebagai cahaya putih (vitt ljussken) atau kilatan putih (vit blixt).
claims.quote: Hennes ande brukar visa sig som ett vitt ljussken eller som en vit blixt.

claims.statement: The present Snogeholm Castle (Snogeholms slott) was built in the late 1860s after the original building (ursprungliga byggnaden) from the 1600s burned down (brunnit ned).
claims.statement_id: Kastel Snogeholm (Snogeholms slott) sekarang dibangun akhir 1860-an setelah bangunan asli (ursprungliga byggnaden) abad ke-17 terbakar (brunnit ned).
claims.quote: Nuvarande Snogeholms slott byggdes i slutet av 1860-talet. Då hade den ursprungliga byggnaden från 1600-talet brunnit ned.

claims.statement: A pågatåg train now bears the name Vita Karin after a naming contest (namntävling) by Skånetrafiken.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah kereta pågatåg kini bernama Vita Karin setelah sayembara nama (namntävling) Skånetrafiken.
claims.quote: Ett pågatåg bär numera namnet "Vita Karin", efter en namntävling på Skånetrafiken.

claims.statement: The waterreus is a figure (personage) of a legend (legende) of the South Holland (Zuid-Hollandse) fishing village (vissersdorp) of Scheveningen, also the name of a family (familie) tied to it.
claims.statement_id: Waterreus adalah tokoh (personage) legenda (legende) desa nelayan (vissersdorp) Scheveningen di Holland Selatan (Zuid-Hollandse), juga nama keluarga (familie) yang terkait legenda itu.
claims.quote: De waterreus is een personage uit een legende uit het Zuid-Hollandse vissersdorp Scheveningen. Daarnaast is het de naam van een familie uit Scheveningen, die aan deze legende verbonden is.

claims.statement: The waterreus was a man or spirit (geest) living in the sea (zee), cursed (vervloekt) to live in the waves (golven); only a girl (meisje) making a cross (kruis) on his forehead (voorhoofd) could save him.
claims.statement_id: Waterreus adalah lelaki atau roh (geest) yang hidup di laut (zee), terkutuk (vervloekt) hidup di ombak (golven); hanya gadis (meisje) yang membuat salib (kruis) di dahinya (voorhoofd) dapat menyelamatkannya.
claims.quote: De waterreus is een manspersoon of geest die vroeger voor Scheveningen in de zee leefde. Hij was vervloekt en gedoemd voor altijd in de golven te leven. Alleen een meisje dat 's nachts met haar wijsvinger een kruis op zijn voorhoofd zou maken, kon hem redden.

claims.statement: A poor widow (weduwe) had a beautiful daughter (dochter) sent fishing (vissen); at first she shunned the spirit (geest), but they fell in love (verliefd).
claims.statement_id: Janda miskin (weduwe) punya putri (dochter) cantik yang disuruh menangkap ikan (vissen); ia mula-mula takut pada roh (geest) itu, tetapi lalu mereka jatuh cinta (verliefd).
claims.quote: Een straatarme weduwe had een beeldschone dochter, die om niet te verhongeren, elke dag uit vissen werd gestuurd. Het meisje moest in het begin niets hebben van de enge geest, maar na verloop van tijd werden ze toch op elkaar verliefd.

claims.statement: The fish (vis) the waterreus drove into her nets (netten) roused jealousy (jaloezie); he came ashore (aan land), they married (trouwden), and their descendants (nageslacht) are called waterreus.
claims.statement_id: Ikan (vis) yang digiring waterreus ke jalanya (netten) membuat warga iri (jaloezie); ia naik ke darat (aan land), mereka menikah (trouwden), dan keturunan (nageslacht) mereka bernama waterreus.
claims.quote: Toen de hoeveelheid vis die de waterreus steeds in haar netten dreef, de jaloezie van de andere dorpsgenoten opwekte, vertelde ze dat ze een bondgenoot in de zee had. Toen de ongelovige dorpsgenoten het zelf uiteindelijk hadden gezien, kwam hij aan land waarna ze trouwden en hun talrijk nageslacht heet sindsdien waterreus.

claims.statement: The Waterreus family (familie) stayed Roman Catholic (rooms-katholiek), never wore local costume (klederdracht), did not turn Protestant (protestant) in the 16th century; the forehead cross is a Catholic symbol (katholiek symbool).
claims.statement_id: Keluarga (familie) Waterreus tetap Katolik Roma (rooms-katholiek), tak memakai pakaian adat (klederdracht), tak menjadi Protestan (protestant) pada abad ke-16; salib di dahi adalah simbol Katolik (katholiek symbool).
claims.quote: Opvallend is dat de Scheveningse familie Waterreus altijd rooms-katholiek is gebleven, nooit de lokale klederdracht heeft gedragen én het zich als voerlui konden veroorloven om niet, zoals de rest van het dorp, in de 16e eeuw protestant te worden. Het kruisje maken op het voorhoofd is, zoals in de legende, een katholiek symbool.

claims.statement: დიხაშ კოჩი („მიწის კაცი“, earth man) is an evil dwarf (ავსული ჯუჯა) of Megrelian mythology (მეგრულ მითოლოგიაში).
claims.statement_id: დიხაშ კოჩი („მიწის კაცი“, manusia tanah) adalah kurcaci jahat (ავსული ჯუჯა) dalam mitologi Megrelia (მეგრულ მითოლოგიაში).
claims.quote: დიხაშ კოჩი (ქართ. „მიწის კაცი“) — ავსული ჯუჯა მეგრულ მითოლოგიაში.

claims.statement: It is the size of a chinka (ჭინკის), human-faced (ადამიანის სახისაა), and moves standing on all fours (ოთხზე დგას).
claims.statement_id: Ukurannya sebesar ჭინკის (chinka), berwajah manusia (ადამიანის სახისაა), dan bergerak dengan empat kaki (ოთხზე დგას).
claims.quote: ტანით ჭინკის ოდენაა, და ჭინკის მსგავსად ადამიანის სახისაა. ეს სახელი იმიტომ ჰქვია, რომ ვერტიკალურად ვერ დადის, და ოთხზე დგას და ისე მოძრაობს.

claims.statement: It appears in villages (სოფლებში) and hides in house yards (სახლის ეზოებშიც); being slow (ნელ-ნელა) it rarely catches its victim (მსხვერპლს).
claims.statement_id: Ia muncul di desa (სოფლებში) dan bersembunyi di halaman rumah (სახლის ეზოებშიც); karena lambat (ნელ-ნელა) ia jarang menangkap korbannya (მსხვერპლს).
claims.quote: ჩნდება ხოლმე სოფლებში, სადაც სახლები მრავლადაა, და ხშირად სახლის ეზოებშიც იმალება ხოლმე. ზოგჯერ კაცს სოფლის გზებზეც ხვდება. რადგან ის ნელ-ნელა მოძრაობს, თავის მსხვერპლს იშვიათად იჭერს

claims.statement: It slips between walkers' legs (ფეხებშუა) to fell them; with a rider (მხედარს) it grabs the bridle (აღვირს) so the horse (ცხენს) cannot step.
claims.statement_id: Ia menyusup di antara kaki (ფეხებშუა) pejalan untuk menjatuhkannya; pada penunggang (მხედარს) ia mencengkeram kekang (აღვირს) sehingga kuda (ცხენს) tak melangkah.
claims.quote: ქვეითად მიმავალთ ფეხებშუა უძვრება და ცდილობს წააქციოს; თუ მხედარს შეხვდა, აღვირს წაავლებს ხელს და ცხენს ფეხის გადადგმის საშუალებას არ აძლევს.

claims.statement: There are cases (შემთხვევებიც) when the დიხაშ კოჩს drove a person (ადამიანი) mad (ჭკუიდან შეუშლია).
claims.statement_id: Ada kejadian (შემთხვევებიც) ketika დიხაშ კოჩს membuat orang (ადამიანი) gila (ჭკუიდან შეუშლია).
claims.quote: არის შემთხვევებიც, როდესაც დიხაშ კოჩს ადამიანი ჭკუიდან შეუშლია.

claims.statement: In German folklore the Weiße Frauen (White Women) are elf-like spirits possibly from Germanic paganism, legends of light elves (Ljósálfar).
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Jerman (German folklore), Weiße Frauen (White Women) adalah roh mirip elf dari paganisme Jermanik (Germanic), legenda elf cahaya (Ljósálfar).
claims.quote: In German folklore, the Weiße Frauen (German: [ˈvaɪsə ˈfʁaʊən] , meaning White Women) are elf-like spirits which may derive from Germanic paganism in the form of legends of light elves (Old Norse: Ljósálfar).

claims.statement: They are beautiful enchanted creatures appearing at noon, brushing their hair in the sunshine or bathing in a brook.
claims.statement_id: Mereka makhluk cantik dan tersihir yang muncul pada tengah hari, menyisir rambut di bawah matahari atau mandi di sungai kecil.
claims.quote: They are described as beautiful and enchanted creatures who appear at noon and can be seen sitting in the sunshine brushing their hair or bathing in a brook.

claims.statement: They may guard treasure or haunt castles, and entreat mortals to break their spell, always unsuccessfully.
claims.statement_id: Mereka menjaga harta atau menghantui kastel, dan memohon manusia mematahkan sihirnya, tetapi selalu gagal.
claims.quote: They may be guarding treasure or haunting castles. They entreat mortals to break their spell, but this is always unsuccessful.

claims.statement: The mythology dates back at least to the Middle Ages and was known in present-day Germany.
claims.statement_id: Mitologi ini setidaknya dari Abad Pertengahan (Middle Ages) dan dikenal di wilayah Jerman (Germany) sekarang.
claims.quote: The mythology dates back at least to the Middle Ages and was known in the present-day area of Germany.

claims.statement: Jacob Grimm traced their whiteness and sunlight to the light elves (Ljósálfar) living in Álfheim under the god Freyr.
claims.statement_id: Jacob Grimm mengaitkan warna putih dan sinar matahari dengan elf cahaya (Ljósálfar) yang tinggal di Álfheim di bawah dewa Freyr.
claims.quote: The association with the color white and their appearance in sunlight is thought by Jacob Grimm to stem from the original Old Norse and Teutonic mythology of alven (elves), specifically the bright Ljósálfar. These "light elves" lived in Álfheim (part of heaven) under the fertility god Freyr.

claims.statement: According to Grimm's Teutonic Mythology, their enchantment may symbolize the ban laid by Christianity on the older gods.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Teutonic Mythology karya Grimm, sihir yang menimpa mereka mungkin lambang larangan Kekristenan (Christianity) atas dewa kepercayaan lama.
claims.quote: According to Grimm's Teutonic Mythology and to the Mythology of All Races Series, the enchantment under which they suffer "may be a symbol of the ban laid by Christianity on the divinities of the older faith."

claims.statement: Counterparts of the Weiße Frauen: the Witte Wieven in the Netherlands, the Dames Blanches in France, and the Low German Witte Wiwer.
claims.statement_id: Padanan Weiße Frauen: Witte Wieven di Belanda (Netherlands), Dames Blanches di Prancis (France), dan Witte Wiwer dalam Jerman Rendah (Low German).
claims.quote: The Weiße Frauen also have counterparts in both name and characterization in neighboring countries: In the Netherlands they are known as the Witte Wieven, and in France as the Dames Blanches. Their Low German equivalent are the Witte Wiwer.

claims.statement: In the Alpine regions of Austria and Southern Germany they are called Salige Frauen or Salige.
claims.statement_id: Di wilayah Alpen (Alpine) Austria dan Jerman Selatan (Southern Germany) mereka disebut Salige Frauen atau Salige.
claims.quote: In the Alpine regions of Austria and Southern Germany they are called Salige Frauen or just Salige (Salkweiber, Salaweiber).

claims.statement: Witte wieven is the name for female figures (vrouwenfiguren) in legends (sagen), sometimes kind (goedaardig), sometimes wicked (kwaadaardig).
claims.statement_id: Witte wieven adalah nama tokoh perempuan (vrouwenfiguren) dalam legenda (sagen) yang kadang baik (goedaardig), kadang jahat (kwaadaardig).
claims.quote: Het is de naam voor vrouwenfiguren die in sagen voorkomen en soms goedaardig, soms kwaadaardig zijn.

claims.statement: Witte wieven are often linked with witches (heksen) or ghosts (spoken).
claims.statement_id: Witte wieven sering dikaitkan dengan penyihir (heksen) atau hantu (spoken).
claims.quote: Witte wieven worden vaak in verband gebracht met heksen of spoken.

claims.statement: Megalithic monuments (Megalithische monumenten) such as burial mounds (grafheuvels) and hunebeds (hunebedden) were seen as the witte wieven's homes (woonsteden).
claims.statement_id: Monumen megalitik (Megalithische monumenten) seperti bukit kubur (grafheuvels) dan hunebed (hunebedden) dianggap tempat tinggal (woonsteden) witte wieven.
claims.quote: Megalithische monumenten als ganggraven, grafheuvels en hunebedden werden door sommigen als hun woonsteden gezien.

claims.statement: Jacob Grimm noted they might come from Holda, Berhta ("white by her very name") and Ostara.
claims.statement_id: Jacob Grimm mencatat mereka mungkin berasal dari Holda, Berhta ("putih menurut namanya"), dan Ostara.
claims.quote: Jacob Grimm noted in particular they might come from Holda, "Berhta, white by her very name" and Ostara.

claims.statement: The Welthund (Bachpfattli in the Oberbaselbiet) is a legendary figure (Sagengestalt) of the German-speaking area (deutschen Sprachraum): a dog (Hund) with one eye (Auge) mid-head (Kopf), lean (mager) in good times, fat in plague (Seuchen) and poverty (Armut).
claims.statement_id: Welthund (Bachpfattli di Oberbaselbiet) adalah tokoh legenda (Sagengestalt) wilayah berbahasa Jerman (deutschen Sprachraum): anjing (Hund) bermata satu (Auge) di tengah kepala (Kopf), kurus (mager) saat makmur, gemuk saat wabah (Seuchen) dan kemiskinan (Armut).
claims.quote: Der Welthund (im Oberbaselbiet Bachpfattli genannt) ist eine Sagengestalt aus dem deutschen Sprachraum. Er wird als Hund beschrieben, der ein Auge „mitten auf dem Kopf“ trägt. Geht es den Bewohnern und Bauern der Landschaft gut, ist er dünn und mager. Plagen Seuchen und Armut das Land, ist er dagegen gut genährt.

claims.statement: Sometimes a wicked lord (bösartiger Landesherr) who tormented farmers (Bauern), condemned by God (Gott) to be the Welthund; sometimes a colonel (Oberst) or ship's captain (Schiffskapitän) who sold his soul (Seele) to the Devil (Teufel).
claims.statement_id: Kadang ia penguasa jahat (bösartiger Landesherr) yang menyiksa petani (Bauern) dan dikutuk Tuhan (Gott) menjadi Welthund; kadang kolonel (Oberst) atau kapten kapal (Schiffskapitän) yang menjual jiwa (Seele) kepada Iblis (Teufel).
claims.quote: Mal war es ein bösartiger Landesherr, der Bauern peinigte und von ihnen übermäßig den Zehnten eintrieb und dafür von Gott dazu verdammt wurde, als Welthund sein weiteres Leben zu fristen, mal war es ein Oberst oder Schiffskapitän, der seine Seele an den Teufel verkaufte.

claims.statement: Nearly all accounts (Schilderungen) say the Welthund appears near moors (Moorlandschaften), swamps (Sümpfen) or rivers (Flussläufen).
claims.statement_id: Hampir semua gambaran (Schilderungen) menyebut Welthund muncul di lahan gambut (Moorlandschaften), rawa (Sümpfen), atau aliran sungai (Flussläufen).
claims.quote: Fast allen Schilderungen des Welthunds gemeinsam ist, dass er bei Moorlandschaften, Sümpfen oder Flussläufen auftritt.

claims.statement: In 2008 the film (Film) Welthund, based on Barbara Saladin's serialized novel (Fortsetzungsroman), ran in northwestern Swiss (Nordwestschweiz) cinemas.
claims.statement_id: Pada 2008 film (Film) Welthund, berdasarkan novel bersambung (Fortsetzungsroman) Barbara Saladin, tayang di bioskop Swiss barat laut (Nordwestschweiz).
claims.quote: 2008 lief in den Kulturkinos der Nordwestschweiz der Film Welthund, der auf dem Fortsetzungsroman „Ein etwas anderer Sommer“ von Barbara Saladin basiert.

claims.statement: The novel (Roman) weaves several Baselbiet legends (Baselbieter Sagen), with the Welthund legend as the film's main plot (Haupthandlungsstrang).
claims.statement_id: Novel (Roman) itu menjalin beberapa legenda Baselbiet (Baselbieter Sagen), dengan legenda Welthund sebagai alur utama (Haupthandlungsstrang) film.
claims.quote: Der Roman verwebt mehrere Baselbieter Sagen zu einer Geschichte, wobei die Sage des Welthunds den Haupthandlungsstrang des Films bildet.

claims.statement: The witte Wiwer, witte Wîwer, witte Wiewer or witte Wiver all mean 'white women' in Low German; Standard German: weiße Weiber.
claims.statement_id: Witte Wiwer, witte Wîwer, witte Wiewer, atau witte Wiver berarti perempuan putih (white women) dalam bahasa Jerman Rendah (Low German); bahasa Jerman baku (Standard German): weiße Weiber.
claims.quote: The witte Wiwer, witte Wîwer, witte Wiewer or witte Wiver ( pronounced [ˈvɪtə ˈviːvɐ] ; all meaning 'white women' in Low German; Standard German: weiße Weiber

claims.statement: They are legendary creatures of (Low) German folklore akin to but distinct from the weiße Frauen, also called unterirdische Weiber in Mecklenburg and Sibyllen in Northwestern Germany.
claims.statement_id: Mereka makhluk legenda cerita rakyat Jerman (German) yang mirip tetapi berbeda dari weiße Frauen, juga disebut unterirdische Weiber di Mecklenburg dan Sibyllen di Jerman barat laut (Northwestern Germany).
claims.quote: are legendary creatures from (Low) German folklore similar to but distinct from the weiße Frauen. Other names are unterirdische Weiber (subterranean women) in Mecklenburg and Sibyllen (sibyls; sg. Sibylle) in Northwestern Germany.

claims.statement: The witte Wiwer of Mecklenburg dwell in the earth, under shrubs, in small hills, forest clearings or beneath old tree roots.
claims.statement_id: Witte Wiwer di Mecklenburg tinggal di tanah, di bawah semak, di bukit kecil, di tanah lapang hutan, atau di bawah akar pohon tua.
claims.quote: The witte Wiwer of Mecklenburg dwell in the earth, under shrubs, in small hills, in forest clearings, or beneath the roots of old trees.

claims.statement: In Westphalia they dwell in the Wittewiwerskule, a pit with a clear spring, or a cave with a door; also in mountains, and on Rügen they use subterranean tunnels.
claims.statement_id: Di Westphalia mereka tinggal di Wittewiwerskule, lubang bermata air jernih, atau gua berpintu; juga di pegunungan, dan di Rügen memakai terowongan bawah tanah.
claims.quote: In Westphalia, the witte Wiwer dwell in a pit with a clear fountain inside surrounded by a grove which is called the Wittewiwerskule (white women's pit), otherwise described as a cave with a door. They are also said to dwell in mountains. On the island of Rügen, they further use subterranean tunnels to get from one place to another.

claims.statement: The witte Wiwer play merry music with fine voices; they exchange unbaptized newborns for changelings (Wechselbälge) if no light burns beside the cradle.
claims.statement_id: Witte Wiwer bermusik riang dan bersuara merdu; mereka menukar bayi belum dibaptis dengan anak ganti (Wechselbälge) bila tak ada lampu di samping buaian.
claims.quote: The witte Wiwer play merry music and have very fine voices. They exchange unbaptized newborn children for changelings (German Wechselbälge, sg. Wechselbalg) if there is no light burning beside the cradle at night, warding them off.

claims.statement: The witte Wiwer borrow the brewing copper at new moon and three evenings later return it filled with their own beer as payment.
claims.statement_id: Witte Wiwer meminjam kuali bir saat bulan baru, lalu tiga malam kemudian mengembalikannya berisi bir buatan mereka sebagai bayaran.
claims.quote: The witte Wiwer might ask to borrow the brewing copper every new moon during twilight hour, taking it away unseen if obliged. Three evenings later, they will return it the very same hour filled with some cans of the beer brewed by them as payment.

claims.statement: They are chased by the wild hunt (wilde Jagd) of the wild huntswoman (wilde Jägerin) Fru Waur and her hounds.
claims.statement_id: Mereka diburu perburuan liar (wild hunt, wilde Jagd) yang dipimpin pemburu perempuan (wilde Jägerin) Fru Waur bersama anjing-anjingnya.
claims.quote: They are chased by the wild hunt (German wilde Jagd) from which they flee with flying hair. The wild hunt consists of the wilde Jägerin (wild huntswoman) and her pack of hounds. The wild huntswoman, known as de oll Fru Waur (the old Lady Waur)

claims.statement: They may carry women just out of childbed to their dwelling and threaten them.
claims.statement_id: Mereka kadang membawa perempuan yang baru melahirkan ke tempat tinggal mereka dan mengancamnya.
claims.quote: They might also take away women just out of childbed and bring them to their dwelling, threatening the woman to stay there or else they would wring her neck.

claims.statement: When the witte Wiwer of Mönchgut on Rügen were driven away their oak withered; they prophesied return when it sprouted again.
claims.statement_id: Ketika witte Wiwer di Mönchgut, Rügen, diusir, pohon ek mereka layu; mereka meramalkan kembali bila pohon itu bertunas lagi.
claims.quote: When the witte Wiwer of Mönchgut in Rügen were driven away, the oak tree connected to them withered. They prophesied their return when the withered oak would sprout again.

claims.statement: The Weiße Frauen article: their Low German equivalent are the Witte Wiwer; in the Netherlands the Witte Wieven.
claims.statement_id: Artikel Weiße Frauen: padanan Jerman Rendah (Low German) mereka adalah Witte Wiwer; di Belanda (Netherlands) Witte Wieven.
claims.quote: In the Netherlands they are known as the Witte Wieven, and in France as the Dames Blanches. Their Low German equivalent are the Witte Wiwer.

claims.statement: The Linton Worm is a mythical beast of a 12th-century Scottish Borders legend; Wyrm is Old English for serpent.
claims.statement_id: Linton Worm adalah makhluk mitos dalam legenda Scottish Borders abad ke-12; Wyrm adalah kata Old English (Inggris Kuno) untuk ular.
claims.quote: The Linton Worm is a mythical beast referred to in a Scottish Borders legend dating back to the 12th century. "Wyrm" is the Old English for serpent.

claims.statement: A 12th-century writer put it at three Scots yards, bigger than a man's leg; the myth resembles the Lambton Worm.
claims.statement_id: Penulis abad ke-12 menggambarkannya sepanjang tiga Scots yards, lebih besar dari kaki manusia; mitos ini mirip Lambton Worm.
claims.quote: A 12th-century writer believed it to be "In length three Scots yards and bigger than an ordinary man’s leg – in form and callour to our common muir edders." The myth is similar to that of the Lambton Worm.

claims.statement: The monster lived in the Worm's Den on Linton Hill, Roxburghshire, emerging at dusk and dawn to eat crops, livestock and people, invulnerable to weapons.
claims.statement_id: Monster itu tinggal di Worm's Den di Linton Hill, Roxburghshire, keluar saat senja dan fajar memakan tanaman, ternak, dan manusia, dan kebal senjata.
claims.quote: The monster lived in a hollow on the northeast side of Linton Hill, a spot still known as the "Worm’s Den", at Linton in Roxburghshire on the Scottish borders. Emerging from its lair at dusk and dawn to ravage the countryside, eating crops, livestock and people, it proved invulnerable to the weapons ranged against it.

claims.statement: The news reached John de Somerville, the reckless Laird of Lariston.
claims.statement_id: Kabar itu sampai kepada John de Somerville, Laird of Lariston yang sangat berani.
claims.quote: The news reached the ears of one John de Somerville, the Laird of Lariston and a man of reckless courage, who was in the south at that time.

claims.statement: As at a joust, De Somerville plunged his burning lance into the monster's mouth and throat, mortally wounding it.
claims.statement_id: Seperti dalam adu tombak, De Somerville menusukkan tombak menyala ke mulut dan kerongkongan monster itu hingga terluka parah.
claims.quote: As if at a joust he attacked it, plunging his burning lance into the monster's gaping mouth and down its throat, mortally wounding it.

claims.statement: The Linton Worm's death throes shaped the hills (wormington); its tail brought the mountain down, burying it.
claims.statement_id: Geliat sekarat Linton Worm membentuk bukit-bukit daerah itu (wormington); ekornya meruntuhkan gunung dan menguburnya.
claims.quote: The writhing death throes of the Linton Worm supposedly created the curious topography of the hills of the region, an area that came to be known as "wormington". The animal retreated to its lair to die, its thrashing tail bringing down the mountain around it and burying it forever.

claims.statement: Folklorist Ernest Marwick notes the Linton worm was slain like the Stoor worm of Orkney, also killed with burning peat.
claims.statement_id: Folklorist Ernest Marwick menyoroti kemiripan cara membunuh Linton worm dengan Stoor worm dari Orkney, yang juga dibunuh dengan gambut menyala.
claims.quote: The Orcadian folklorist Ernest Marwick highlights the similarity between the method used to kill the Linton worm and those recounted in the slaying of the Stoor worm of Orkney, which was also killed with burning peat.

claims.statement: He was made Royal Falconer, knighted and First Barrone of Linton; the Somervilles' crest was a wyvern on a wheel.
claims.statement_id: De Somerville menjadi Royal Falconer, kesatria, dan First Barrone Linton; lambang Somervilles adalah wyvern di atas roda.
claims.quote: He was made Royal Falconer, knighted and made "First Barrone" of Linton. The crest of the Somervilles was a wyvern (heraldic dragon) perched on a wheel.

claims.statement: In the 12th century Linton was terrorised by a dragon-like monster called The Linton Worm.
claims.statement_id: Pada abad ke-12 daerah Linton diteror monster mirip naga (dragon-like) bernama The Linton Worm.
claims.quote: During the 12th century, the area of Linton was being terrorised by a dragon-like monster known as The Linton Worm.

claims.statement: The church porch door bears the "Somervail Stone" of a knight fighting two beasts, linked to the Worm of Linton.
claims.statement_id: Pintu serambi gereja Linton dipasangi "Somervail Stone" bergambar kesatria melawan dua binatang, terkait kisah Worm of Linton.
claims.quote: The porch door has been inset with the "Somervail Stone" showing a knight fighting two beasts which is a link to the story of the Worm of Linton.

claims.statement_id: Lagerlöf: dahulu di Närke ada sesuatu yang tak ditemukan di tempat lain, yaitu penyihir (witch) bernama Ysätter-Kaisa.
claims.quote: In bygone days there was something in Närke the like of which was not to be found elsewhere: it was a witch, named Ysätter-Kaisa.

claims.statement: In Lagerlöf's portrayal Ysätters-Kajsa was not a gloomy troll but happy and playful.
claims.statement_id: Dalam penggambaran Lagerlöf, Ysätters-Kajsa bukan troll muram melainkan riang dan suka bermain.
claims.quote: Ysätters-Kajsa was not a dark and gloomy troll, but a happy and playful one.

claims.statement: She was named Kaisa because of her dealings with wind and storm, as wind witches are called; the surname came from Ysätter swamp in Asker parish.
claims.statement_id: Nama Kaisa diberikan karena ia berurusan dengan angin dan badai (wind and storm), sebutan penyihir angin (wind witches); julukan dari rawa Ysätter (Ysätter swamp) di paroki Asker.

claims.statement: She stood in the centre of the whirlwind, her hair whirling among the clouds, her skirt dragging like a dust storm.
claims.statement_id: Ia berdiri di tengah angin puyuh (whirlwind), rambutnya berputar di antara awan (clouds), roknya menyeret seperti badai debu (dust storm).
claims.quote: She would then stand in the centre of the whirlwind. Her long hair would whirl among the clouds, while her skirt would drag on the ground like a dust storm.

claims.statement: Ysätters-Kajsa was not a gloomy troll but a happy, playful one who most liked a real gale.
claims.statement_id: Ysätters-Kajsa bukan troll muram, melainkan riang dan suka bermain (playful), dan paling menyukai angin badai (gale).
claims.quote: Ysätters-Kajsa was not a dark and gloomy troll, but a happy and playful one. What she liked most was a real gale.

claims.statement: She was hardest on the quarrelsome and wicked, but cared for honest folk and poor children.
claims.statement_id: Ia paling keras terhadap orang yang suka bertengkar dan jahat, tetapi melindungi orang jujur dan anak-anak miskin.
claims.quote: People noticed that she was hardest on people who were quarrelsome, mean and wicked, but she would often take honest folks and small poor children into her care.

claims.statement: Old people said that when the church of Asker burned, Ysätters-Kajsa nestled among the smoke and fire on its roof and put it out.
claims.statement_id: Orang tua bercerita bahwa ketika gereja Asker terbakar, Ysätters-Kajsa bersarang di asap dan api di atapnya lalu memadamkannya.
claims.quote: Old people used to say that once, when the church of Asker was burning, Ysätters-Kajsa came, nestled herself among the smoke and fire on the roof of the church, and put it out.

claims.statement: In winter she started a storm and piled snow drifts high.
claims.statement_id: Di musim dingin ia menimbulkan badai (storm) dan timbunan salju (snow drifts) tinggi.
claims.quote: Then she would start a real storm and create snow drifts so high that people could hardly get home in the evening.

claims.statement: Lagerlöf ends her portrait: people now claim Ysätters-Kajsa is dead like all other trolls, but that is almost impossible to believe.
claims.statement_id: Lagerlöf menutup penggambarannya: kini orang berkata Ysätters-Kajsa sudah mati seperti troll lain, tetapi hal itu hampir mustahil dipercaya.
claims.quote: Lagerlöf finishes her presentation of the troll by saying: "Nowadays, people claim that Ysätters-Kajsa is dead and gone, like all other trolls, but such things are almost impossible to believe.

claims.statement: Lagerlöf: old people say that when Asker church burned, Ysätter-Kaisa lit on the roof amid fire and smoke and averted disaster.
claims.statement_id: Lagerlöf: orang tua bercerita ketika gereja Asker (Asker church) terbakar, Ysätter-Kaisa hinggap di atap di tengah api dan asap dan mencegah bencana.
claims.quote: Old people say of her that, once, when Asker church was burning, Ysätter-Kaisa swept through the air, lit amid fire and smoke on the church roof, and averted the disaster.

claims.statement: The ziphius is a fabulous beast (fabeldier), a water owl (wateruil) as big as a whale (walvis) with a V-shaped beak (snavel) and huge mouth (mond).
claims.statement_id: Ziphius adalah hewan dongeng (fabeldier), burung hantu air (wateruil) sebesar paus (walvis) berparuh (snavel) V dan bermulut (mond) besar.
claims.quote: De ziphius is een fabeldier. Het is een wateruil zo groot als een walvis, met een V-vormige snavel en een enorme mond.

claims.statement: It attacks every ship (schip) that comes near (in de buurt komt).
claims.statement_id: Ia menyerang setiap kapal (schip) yang mendekat (in de buurt komt).
claims.quote: Het valt elk schip aan dat in de buurt komt.

claims.statement: The ziphius gave its name (naamgever) to the Dolfijn van Cuvier (Ziphius cavirostris).
claims.statement_id: Ziphius adalah pemberi nama (naamgever) bagi Dolfijn van Cuvier (Ziphius cavirostris).
claims.quote: De ziphius is de naamgever van de Dolfijn van Cuvier (Lat. Ziphius cavirostris).
